analysis.title: GOAL: Global Opportunity Asset Locator: Giving credit to balance — bonds gradually moving from headwind to hedge
key_insights: GS shifts back to overweight equities on a 3m horizon, in line with its 12m overweight. Earnings growth stays supportive and the valuation de-rating since the summer improves asymmetry into Q3 earnings season.
GS shifts to overweight bonds on a 12m horizon and stays neutral on a 3m horizon. Tactically it prefers shorter-duration fixed income and is overweight cash for 3m.

Bonds should gradually move from a portfolio headwind to a hedge. Higher carry, better return asymmetry and lower expected inflation support more normal strategic bond allocations, while higher yields, fiscal concerns, AI capital competition and inflation uncertainty argue for tactical caution on duration.

GS goes underweight credit for 3m, in line with its 12m allocation, and prefers equities over credit. For the USD IG index the credit spread is only 15% of the yield versus a 45% recent average, and releveraging and supply remain headwinds.

Risky assets consolidated since the summer as rates and energy-price headwinds replaced earnings tailwinds. Small and mid caps, real estate, infrastructure and bond-proxy sectors were pressured, and credit spreads and Euro area sovereign spreads (France/OAT) widened.

MSCI AC World 12-month forward P/E has fallen nearly 20% year to date, an unusually large late-cycle de-rating. Strong earnings growth tied to the AI capex boom has cushioned global equities against higher yields.

Equity regional stance: overweight Asia/US, underweight Europe. GS likes a barbell of global Tech with selective rate-sensitive, low-vol, high-dividend, bond-proxy stocks that have de-rated since the summer.

The US team still expects 18% S&P 500 earnings growth in 2027 excluding revaluation of equity stakes, and 11% in both 2027 and 2028 including it. GS expects Q3 earnings to surprise to the upside in the US and Europe.

The bond sell-off was led by front-end and real yields rather than term premia, steeper curves or breakevens. Market pricing is more hawkish than GS economists' baseline: more than three further Fed hikes, at least two from the ECB and nearly four from the BoE, versus GS's one more hike each from the ECB and BoE.

The Risk Appetite Indicator has fallen to zero from elevated levels over the past two weeks. RAI PC2 (monetary policy) is at one of its lowest levels since 2000. Across 11 prior PC2 troughs since 2000 the S&P 500 typically corrected then resumed its uptrend and US 10y yields stayed rangebound, except in 2022.

Macro baseline is Goldilocks-like: stable growth near trend, low US recession risk, inflation score near peak and falling in 2027, which limits central bank tightening. The US economy is bifurcated, strong among upper-income consumers and AI-exposed sectors, weaker in housing and consumer spending.

The DAA model signals less downside risk for 60/40 portfolios over the next 12 months under the macro baseline. The model does not capture AI capex earnings tailwinds and may understate equity upside.

Commodities stay neutral. Dec26 Brent is above $100/bbl on Iranian attacks on tankers, and refined products and TTF gas are near YTD highs. GS lowered its year-end gold target to $4,650/toz from $4,900/toz but keeps a $5,400/toz end-2027 target on central bank buying.

Commodities team recommends hedging geopolitical risk through long 2027 European gasoline positions, and sees TTF possibly reaching 150 EUR/MWh by year-end if Persian Gulf LNG exports don't improve and winter is colder than average.

Cross-asset implied vol is low, with VIX at 15, and implied correlations are near historical lows because of high dispersion, which makes equity upside hedges and call options inexpensive. The MOVE-to-VIX ratio is at its highest since 2024.

Hedging recommendations: VIX call spreads, front-end receiver swaptions as a convex recession hedge, puts on EUR/USD and EUR/CHF for Euro area fiscal risk, and selling back-end rate payers to fund equity puts.

sector_views.rationale: Strong earnings growth from the AI capex boom drove the de-rating in hardware, and AI application and adoption is expanding valuations for AI revenue beneficiaries.
Selective exposure as the other side of a barbell, since these stocks de-rated since summer and could benefit from rate relief.
Suffered outright drawdowns since the summer from rising yields without earnings support, though bond proxies are included in the selective barbell.
Rate-sensitive areas like small and mid caps suffered from rising yields.
Precious metals preferred within a neutral commodities allocation, supported by central bank diversification.

earnings_insights: Q3 earnings season is expected to surprise to the upside in both the US and Europe, per GS equity strategy teams.
GS US team expects S&P 500 earnings growth of 11% in both 2027 and 2028, and 18% in 2027 excluding base effects from revaluation of equity stakes.

Companies are 'over-earning' because of gains on private investment stakes and margin expansion for semiconductor and memory companies tied to the AI capex boom. The gap between S&P 500 earnings growth and US nominal GDP growth is likely to stay among the widest since the 1980s.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports the overweight equities call even as growth moderates.
Earnings growth stays healthy and well above nominal GDP growth.
Market pricing is more hawkish than GS's baseline, which leaves room for rate relief if inflation normalises.
GS economists expect only one more ECB hike, with potential cuts beginning next year.
GS economists expect only one more BoE hike, with potential cuts beginning next year.
GS forecasts yields falling 49-78bp, which supports the 12m overweight in US 10y bonds.
Yield decline supports overweight UK gilts at 12m.
Smaller expected decline, consistent with the underweight Japan bond stance.
GS expects energy prices to normalise into year-end, which supports the inflation-easing baseline.
Central bank diversification is the main structural driver, though a hawkish Fed may weigh on ETF demand near term.
Low implied vol keeps equity upside hedges and call options inexpensive.
Sturdy US growth, in line with the Goldilocks baseline.

trade_ideas.description: Use call options to add selectively to equities while keeping tactical cash balances
trade_ideas.rationale: Equity upside hedges are inexpensive because dispersion keeps index vol and implied correlations low.
trade_ideas.risk: Rates volatility, Middle East tensions and US midterm uncertainty could keep markets volatile.

trade_ideas.description: Buy VIX call spreads (3m) as a broad downside hedge into year-end
trade_ideas.rationale: Max-payoff ratios are high relative to history, and the VIX is low versus other risk measures such as CDS spreads.
trade_ideas.risk: Dispersion has kept the VIX low, and the hedge only pays if a macro shock drives correlations sharply higher.

trade_ideas.description: Buy front-end receiver swaptions (12m 25-delta on 1y or 2y USD rates) as a recession hedge
trade_ideas.rationale: Front-end forward rates have risen sharply YTD, and receivers benefit from the central-bank put in a downturn and from rate relief if energy prices decline.

trade_ideas.description: Sell payers on back-end rates to fund equity puts
trade_ideas.rationale: Further sharp rises in yields would weigh more on equities than bonds, and rates vol is elevated relative to equity vol.

trade_ideas.description: Buy puts on EUR/USD and EUR/CHF to hedge Euro area fiscal risk
trade_ideas.rationale: A targeted hedge against rising Euro area sovereign risk premia.
trade_ideas.risk: Less likely to pay off unless sovereign stress broadens across the region.

trade_ideas.description: Long 2027 positions in European gasoline to hedge geopolitical risk
trade_ideas.rationale: Refined products remain near YTD highs and persistent pressure on gasoline and diesel is a concern.

risk_factors: Higher rates and energy prices are the main near-term downside risk to equities.
Further sharp rises in yields (more than two standard deviations over three months) have historically been challenging for equity returns.
Fiscal concerns, AI-related capital competition and inflation uncertainty argue for tactical caution on duration.
Credit spread risks to the credit strategy team's year-end forecasts are tilted toward more widening, with continued supply and releveraging.
Durability of earnings for AI infrastructure stocks, and a more serious de-risking in Tech, could cause the barbell to decouple.
Euro area sovereign stress, particularly in France, could broaden.
US midterm election uncertainty could lift equity volatility from current low levels.
A hawkish Fed might weigh on ETF demand for gold in the near term.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 sets the asset allocation table: 3m and 12m weights show OW equities, OW bonds (12m) and OW cash (3m), UW credit.
Exhibit 15 shows global equities de-rated materially, with 12m forward P/E ratios down 20%.
Exhibit 17 shows the return decomposition since June 2026 into earnings, valuations, FX and price change for AI-related baskets and indices.
Exhibit 19 shows 3m implied correlation within and across S&P 500 sectors as extremely low.
vol_and_positioning: VIX is at 15 and FX vol is similarly anchored. Credit implied vol has picked up but remains low relative to history.

Implied correlations are close to historical lows within and across S&P 500 sectors, driven by high dispersion. Index vol is contained and equity upside hedges into year-end are inexpensive, particularly in rate-sensitive areas.
Rates vol has risen sharply over the summer, pushing the MOVE-to-VIX ratio to its highest since 2024, though it has started to reset.
VIX call spreads are attractive as broad downside hedges into year-end, with max-payoff ratios high relative to history. The VIX is also low relative to other risk measures such as CDS spreads.

Front-end receiver swaptions (12m 25-delta on 1y or 2y USD rates) offer a more convex recession hedge. In previous recessions a receiver swaption would have paid more than an out-of-the-money S&P 500 put.
Tactically, sell payers on back-end rates to fund equity puts.
Puts on EUR/USD and EUR/CHF are a targeted hedge against Euro area fiscal risk, but less likely to pay off unless sovereign stress broadens.
The Risk Appetite Indicator has fallen to zero, and RAI PC2 is at one of its lowest levels since 2000. The RAI credit subcomponent had one of its sharpest weekly declines since 2000.
geopolitical: Middle East tensions and Iranian attacks on tankers keep Dec26 Brent above $100/bbl.
Persian Gulf oil exports (including 'dark exports') are back to pre-war levels, but Persian Gulf LNG exports remain a risk for TTF gas.
US midterm election uncertainty may lift equity volatility from current low levels.
Euro area sovereign risk is being repriced, with French OAT spreads widening.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher carry and reinvestment yields, improving asymmetry for long-duration bonds, and a macro baseline of inflation normalisation and less hawkish central banks let bonds recover diversification benefits over 12 months.
tension_points.bear_case: Fiscal concerns, AI capex financing competition, sticky inflation and Middle East energy risk keep yields volatile, so added duration may add volatility rather than cushion portfolios near term.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Yield increases exceeding two standard deviations over three months, which have historically been challenging for equity returns, or inflation momentum failing to decline.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong earnings growth, 18% S&P 500 EPS growth expected in 2027 ex-revaluation gains, has let equities buffer higher yields, and the 20% P/E de-rating improves asymmetry.
tension_points.bear_case: Further sharp rises in yields and energy prices would weigh on equities, and rate-sensitive areas without earnings support are already in drawdown.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A continued sharp increase in bond yields (more than two standard deviations over three months) or energy prices rising further.

tension_points.bull_case: Credit year-end spread tightening is typical in late December as supply slows, and spreads are close to the credit team's year-end targets.
tension_points.bear_case: Spreads are tight relative to all-in yields, with releveraging and supply headwinds, and risks to the credit team's forecasts are tilted toward widening.
